status: Pi 1.3.0 isRetryableAssistantError and the Fabric failover compaction decision layer ported and differentially verified against the unchanged upstream TypeScript and Pi dist; Fabric execution itself (pi-fabric) remains out of scope

upstreamSpecTests.note: 6 it declarations (one it.each with 2 cases = 7 executions). All 7 are covered: quota two-account rotation, auth rotation, fabric-absent rotation, transient surface+compact, exhausted-once, visible output, aborted run.

rustTests.failover_cases_match_the_upstream_refere: tests/fabric.rs (29 cases, complete JSON, driven through the real lift::run)
rustTests.handled_passthrough_and_fabric_availabil: tests/fabric.rs (absent/throwing tool listing, non-retryable and missing message)

checks.mutationChecks: Removing the non-retryable precedence failed both classifier tests; dropping the JavaScript dot rewrite (rate\nlimit, rate\rlimit, rate\u2028limit, rate\u2029limit) failed the classifier test; changing the debounce window to 0, lowering the enabled-account threshold from 2 to 1, and disabling the retryable guard each failed the failover test. All sources were restored and re-verified before commit.

compared: isRetryableAssistantError for every upstream pattern sample, every documented real-world message, case variants, quota-over-transient precedence, non-error stop reasons, missing and empty errorMessage, and JavaScript dot semantics across \n, \r, U+2028 and U+2029 (complete case objects: name, message, result)
Fabric availability detection: fabric_exec present, absent, and a throwing tool listing (complete expected object per case)

handleFailover claim decisions with and without fabric, for retryable, quota, auth, empty and missing messages, visible output, and aborted runs, including the external-integration verdict passthrough

runFailoverCompaction guards: 30 s debounce (10 s, 29.999 s suppressed; exactly 30 s allowed), >=2 enabled accounts (1 enabled and 2-with-1-disabled skip), throwing pool snapshot, missing pool, idle wait then compact, 15 s idle timeout (300 polls), and compaction completion notice versus silent failure

The complete per-case projection: handled, attempts, event types, compactCalls, notify pairs, accountsQueried and 50 ms poll count, with attempts and events produced by the real ported lift state machine
limits: Fabric execution (pi-fabric's deterministic compaction engine) is out of scope; the decision layer stops at ctx.compact() and its onComplete/onError callbacks, which the injected FabricHost models as CompactOutcome.
The native service binding (Pi ExtensionContext -> FabricHost, and spawning the compaction task) is a later lane. decide_failover is the integration point for lift::Host::failover.

The second debounce re-check after the idle wait is unreachable in a serialized replay: the initial check requires startedAt - last >= 30 s and the re-check compares a later timestamp against the same value, so it can only fire when a concurrent compaction updates last during the wait. The upstream line is ported verbatim and covered by inspection, not by a scenario.

Upstream could not reach info.failure.assistantMessage === undefined through the lift: thrown setup errors rotate inline without calling onFailover. That branch is covered by the Rust-only handled_passthrough_and_fabric_availability test (None message) instead.

A pool with zero enabled accounts never installs a lifted provider, so the >=2 guard is only reachable with 1 or 2-with-1-disabled accounts; the missing-pool branch is covered by the Rust-only guard test.

JavaScript /i case folding is not identical to the regex crate's Unicode-aware (?i) for characters such as U+212A and U+017F; the classifier corpus is ASCII plus the dot-semantics characters where both agree, and every error string the upstream comments and specs name is ASCII.

The upstream extension is driven with a scripted ExtensionAPI/ExtensionContext and an injected clock; MultiProviderService.prototype.snapshot is wrapped in memory (never on disk) to observe the pool lookup and to script a throwing snapshot. No real time, network, credential or ~/.pi access occurs.
